releases.title: Multi-user accounts and README demo
changes: Added the supplied BallerWatch screenshot to the repository README as the demo image.
Added multi-user sign-in with usernames, independent passwords, per-user pickup RSVP names, per-user session revisions, and backward-compatible migration of the existing account to admin.
Added administrator-only user creation/removal and kept monitored league teams shared and administrator-controlled.
Changed RSVP confirmation and signed-in Q&A personalization to use the active user's RSVP name rather than one global identity.
Changed password updates, session revocation, and GitHub Actions password recovery to target one username without revoking other users.
Bumped the PWA asset revision to 6.1.0 for the new Settings/login UI.
Finalized the 6.1.0 release candidate at the exact validated head after aligning the encrypted-state regression assertion with the multi-user settings write path.

releases.title: Glass app icon and feedback-driven Q&A polish
changes: Redesigned the BallerWatch favicon/PWA icon as a layered glass tile with cyan/green refraction, subtle highlights, and a high-contrast soccer mark that remains readable at small sizes.

Applied the same glass icon to the in-app header and refreshed the iPhone apple-touch icon, manifest reference, and service-worker asset revision so installed clients pick it up instead of retaining the old flat icon.

Improved generic dated detail routing so natural questions such as “what time Thursday?” can use the combined game view while preserving terse pickup shortcuts such as “Thursday time”, /time, /field, and /count.
Added deterministic privacy-safe wrong-answer fingerprints and more specific Q&A/weather feature-request aggregate categories without exposing retained private question text.
Confirmed the 6.0.10 release candidate at the corrected, fully validated head so production promotion includes the glass-icon regression fix.

releases.title: Zero-AI smart Q&A and contextual autocomplete
changes: Changed normal Q&A routing to a deterministic local parser so supported pickup, schedule, opponent, jersey, time, venue, team, and version questions do not call an external AI classifier.
Added context-aware follow-up handling so short questions such as “what color?”, “who do we play?”, “where is it?”, and “what time?” reuse the previously referenced game date.
Added targeted date-game answers for opponent, jersey, time, venue, and pickup RSVP/capacity questions instead of requiring exact canned wording.
Expanded deterministic intent matching with more natural phrasing and one-edit typo tolerance for meaningful words.
Rebuilt autocomplete from upcoming calendar data, broader question templates, and private on-device recent successful questions; matching now accepts word reordering and small typos.

Removed redundant GitHub Actions workflows for stale branch cleanup, standalone manual smoke, and duplicate standalone weather refresh; weather remains covered by schedule-change refreshes and the watchdog.
Aligned the 6.0.9 service-worker revision and regression coverage after the Q&A/autocomplete changes so the fixed release candidate is fully validation-gated.

releases.title: Gesture feedback, jersey-detail routing, and sign-in throttling
changes: Removed the visible Wrong answer button. Double-clicking an answer on desktop or pressing and holding it on touch now marks that exact answer wrong; repeating the gesture cancels the feedback.
Fixed dated jersey questions such as “what jersey color do I wear for 10/6” so they route deterministically to the matching game details even when the word “game” is omitted.

Hardened password sign-in throttling by counting failures against both a hashed IP bucket and a hashed IP-plus-user-agent bucket, keeping the existing 10-failure / roughly 10-minute automatic lockout without persisting raw IP addresses.
Added Retry-After metadata for rate-limited sign-in responses.

releases.title: Reviewed Q&A date routing, weekly schedules, and feedback collection
changes: Fixed pickup date routing so explicit weekday/date questions never fall back to a previous conversation date or a different sole future pickup; if no pickup exists on the requested day, the answer stays on that day.
Added deterministic multi-game schedule answers for this week, next week, the coming week, and next N weeks across pickup and monitored league matches.

Restored signed-in feature-request collection: /feature requests and unsupported signed-in Q&A are stored only in encrypted requests/private.json while requests/unknown.json remains a category/count-only encrypted projection.

Improved chat history/review fallback so answer intent survives when AI compaction is unavailable, Wrong answer feedback identifies the original Q&A intent, and operational/unsupported failures can still become actionable review signals.
Moved privacy-safe feature-request category/projection logic into a runtime-agnostic shared module used by both Node workflows and the Cloudflare Worker.

releases.title: Wider web layout, match freshness, and copyright
changes: Widened the desktop website to a 920px landscape-friendly content area while keeping mobile responsive.
Changed Notifications, Settings, and notification detail to open centered within the same main website footprint instead of using a narrow portrait-only surface.
Added a subtle source refresh line to match cards using the pickup source-health check time or the RATS schedule refresh time, separate from the weather refresh timestamp.
Added visible application copyright text, source-file copyright headers, a repository COPYRIGHT.md notice, and a README copyright section without introducing a new software license.
Bumped web and PWA asset revisions so deployed clients revalidate the 6.0.6 layout immediately.

releases.title: Portrait navigation, card-only calendar expansion, swipe waterfall, and RSVP state
changes: Removed the explicit calendar Expand/Collapse button; a single click on the calendar card now toggles between the rolling 14-day view and the full schedule through the latest published match week.

Changed Home, Notifications, notification detail, Settings, and install surfaces to share one centered iPhone-like portrait viewport on desktop and mobile instead of letting notification surfaces float in the wider landscape browser area.
Refined desktop match-card left/right affordances so their overlay fits the match-card border exactly and uses pointer-distance-driven opacity with a blurred edge-to-transparent waterfall gradient.

Changed pickup RSVP styling so the button matches Directions/Share by default and turns green with a check only when the authenticated user's saved RSVP name is actually present in the private confirmed player roster.
Added an authenticated RSVP-status endpoint that exposes only confirmed/waitlisted dates, never roster names, and added regression coverage for the privacy boundary and UI state.

releases.title: Settings authentication hotfix
changes: Restored the missing web user capability verifier used by Settings, password change, session revoke, and authenticated feedback routes, eliminating the Cloudflare 1101 exception that surfaced in Safari as Load failed.
Kept user session revocation semantics by validating bearer tokens against the current encrypted web authentication revision before allowing authenticated web actions.
Added regression coverage for empty, current-revision, and revoked-revision capability tokens.

releases.title: Expandable calendar, reliable Settings, pickup RSVP, and web layout polish
changes: Changed the 14-day match calendar into a rolling two-week window that advances by week when spotlight navigation reaches a later match, with one-tap expansion through the final week containing a published future match.

Hardened web Settings loading and saving with structured CORS-safe load failures, a refreshed runtime-state file revision between user and team writes, and one retry for transient browser network failures such as Safari's Load failed error.
Added a pickup RSVP action on pickup match cards that opens the public RSVP site with the selected pickup date preselected.
Changed the website Home Screen app prompt to use the same card spacing, radius, glass treatment, and responsive layout as the rest of the dashboard.
Bumped static PWA asset revisions so website and installed-app clients revalidate the 6.0.3 UI immediately.

releases.title: Full future league schedule navigation
changes: Changed the web calendar payload so every future published RATS league match remains available to the installed web app instead of being truncated to the 14-day weather window.
Changed spotlight arrow and swipe navigation to traverse all future published league match dates while keeping the visible weather calendar strip at 14 days.
Added regression coverage proving league matches beyond the 14-day weather window remain available while far-future pickup entries stay bounded to that window.

releases.title: Runtime watcher recovery and scheduler credential validation
changes: Changed RATS schedule reconciliation so aggregate-only future events that are absent from the team’s published export no longer freeze the entire league snapshot; every published export game must still match exactly once and export-backed disagreements continue to fail closed.
Added regression coverage for aggregate-only unpublished RATS events while preserving strict validation for published matches.
Added a non-mutating GitHub Actions credential check before cron-job.org synchronization so an invalid CRON_GITHUB_PAT fails before scheduler jobs are updated.

releases.title: Web-only BallerWatch runtime
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 6 moves fully to the web app, with Web Push notifications and repository-admin password recovery.
changes: Removed the retired messaging adapter, inbound webhook route, listener workflow, adapter source modules, credentials, tests, documentation, scheduler compatibility code, and app shortcut.
Renamed the Cloudflare service to ballerwatch-web and moved its source to infra/web-worker; the PWA and service worker now use the new web-only endpoint.

Replaced pairing-code bootstrap/recovery with the manual Reset web user password workflow backed by a temporary BALLERWATCH_RECOVERY_PASSWORD Actions secret; resets advance the authentication revision and revoke older sessions.

Moved canonical encrypted user settings to state/user.json and added a release migration that reads the previous encrypted user-state file once, rewrites the new canonical path, and compacts the obsolete path away.
Changed pickup, league, and release notifications to Web Push/notification-board only; tests, smoke, deployment, and health checks remain notification-silent.
Changed authenticated Settings and answer-feedback persistence to write encrypted runtime state directly through the web Worker rather than dispatching a legacy listener workflow.

Changed release rollout ordering so the web Worker must deploy and pass live runtime/security readiness before GitHub Pages is dispatched, reducing the chance of publishing a PWA that points at an unavailable API.
Added regression coverage to prevent the retired messaging integration, old credentials, webhook route, and removed source/workflow paths from being reintroduced.

releases.title: Web Push SSRF closure and authentication hardening
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.8.2 hardens Web Push registration, recovery pairing, user sessions, browser policies, workflow dependencies, and cryptographic key separation.
changes: Closed the delayed blind Web Push SSRF path by allowing only recognized browser push-service hosts, rejecting IP literals/userinfo/nonstandard ports, validating every DNS answer as public before GitHub Actions delivery, and disabling HTTP redirects.

Added a short-lived server-issued Web Push registration challenge bound to the normalized endpoint, exact PWA-origin checks, and registration rate limits before subscription events can enter encrypted runtime state.

Changed legacy pairing command recovery from six numeric reusable digits to a 12-character high-entropy human-readable code that is single-use, expires after 10 minutes, and is protected by per-client failed-attempt limits.
Added server-side authentication revisions to the 90-day user capability tokens; password changes revoke prior sessions and Settings now includes an explicit Sign out all devices action.

Separated cryptographic domains for runtime encryption, user-token signing, feedback-token signing, password verification, and push-registration challenges; deployment transparently reads legacy encrypted state and reseals it under the new runtime key domain.

Added Worker security headers, a restrictive document CSP/referrer policy for the GitHub Pages PWA, and service-worker navigation checks that refuse notification destinations outside the BallerWatch Pages path.
Pinned every GitHub Actions dependency to a reviewed 40-character commit SHA instead of mutable major-version tags.

Added regression coverage for malicious push URLs, private/link-local addresses, redirect behavior, mixed DNS answers/rebinding, pairing entropy/single use, token revisions, key migration, security policies, service-worker navigation, and workflow pinning.

releases.title: Runtime-state recovery and trustworthy live health
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.8.1 restores web game/calendar data and makes the Live indicator reflect real runtime readiness.
changes: Separated GitHub runtime-state content access from workflow dispatch credentials so the Worker uses the dedicated release/content token for encrypted state reads and writes instead of the scheduler dispatch token.
Changed Worker health and web config readiness to fail when encrypted runtime-state cannot be loaded, rather than reporting a healthy shell while game data is unavailable.
Changed the web app Live indicator to require successful runtime-backed calendar and notification-board reads; failed data loads now remain visibly Offline.

Expanded Worker deployment smoke tests to verify the dedicated content credential plus live /health, /web/config, /web/next-game, /web/calendar, and expected PWA CORS behavior before a deployment is considered healthy.
Added regression coverage for credential separation, runtime-backed readiness, and truthful client health status.

releases.title: User-first settings, fully encrypted runtime state, and interaction polish
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.8 makes Settings user-first, encrypts every runtime-state file, softens desktop carousel edge navigation, and adds a blurred iPhone status-area layer.
changes: Changed app-facing authentication language from owner to user and moved the PWA to /web/user routes while retaining legacy owner routes and existing device tokens for compatibility.

Made every canonical file on runtime-state a complete AES-GCM envelope, including listener metadata, engineering review signals, and feature-summary projections; deployment migrates legacy files and refuses unencrypted writes.
Added recurring runtime-state encryption audits so a readable canonical payload fails deployment/maintenance checks instead of silently persisting.
Redesigned desktop match-card navigation as wide transparent edge hit zones with a soft blurred glow and borderless arrow cue, while preserving the connected-card carousel animation.
Added an installed-iPhone status-area glass layer so scrolling content is visually separated from the Dynamic Island and system status icons.

Carried forward the useful retired-watchdog dispatch guard from the stale 5.0.2 branch and simplified external-cron setup to a manual recovery workflow because normal Worker deployment already owns scheduler synchronization.
Added support for a dedicated RELEASE_GITHUB_TOKEN for GitHub Release publication while retaining CRON_GITHUB_PAT as a compatibility fallback.
Refactored runtime storage documentation, tests, and onboarding around explicit main/production/runtime-state boundaries and future scale.

releases.title: Release-gated rollout, desktop carousel controls, and owner sign-in
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.7 adds desktop carousel edge navigation, app-native owner sign-in, and a safer release-gated production rollout.
changes: Added subtle previous/next controls to the desktop match carousel: moving the pointer onto an available card edge reveals a glass arrow, and one click advances the same connected-card train animation used by touch swipes.
Added app-native owner password sign-in for Settings so normal use on new devices no longer requires a legacy pairing command code after the owner password is configured.
Kept legacy pairing command as a first-time bootstrap and recovery option; paired devices can set or rotate the owner password from Settings.
Stores only a server-keyed salted password verifier inside encrypted runtime state; plaintext owner passwords are never persisted or sent through GitHub Actions.

Introduced a production branch and GitHub Release promotion gate so merging product code to main no longer deploys the Pages app, Worker, Calendar bridge, weather bootstrap, or web runtime immediately.

Added an hourly production eligibility check that requires a green validation run and at least a 24-hour candidate soak before publishing the version's GitHub Release; manual promotion can publish the validated version immediately.
Pinned watcher, listener, watchdog, and external scheduler runtime execution to the promoted production branch so unreleased main code does not silently become production behavior.

Changed repository versioning policy so documentation-only changes, behavior-preserving refactors, tests, CI/workflow maintenance, formatting, and other internal housekeeping do not receive a new SemVer version.

Decoupled the PWA/Worker from mandatory legacy messaging credentials: owner-authenticated web settings, public-safe Q&A, Web Push, and core Worker deployment can remain available with the legacy messaging adapter disabled.

releases.title: Frictionless feedback and multi-device pairing
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.6 makes wrong-answer feedback one tap on mobile without opening Settings, lets one legacy pairing command code authorize multiple devices for 10 minutes, and restores autocomplete as a floating dropdown.
changes: Decoupled wrong-answer feedback from owner settings: each successful web answer now carries a short-lived signed feedback token scoped to that exact question/answer, so marking an answer wrong does not grant or require owner-settings access.
Added a visible one-tap Wrong answer / Undo wrong answer control for mobile while retaining desktop double-click as a shortcut.
Prevented long-press selection/copy on the answer surface and used touch-action manipulation so the feedback interaction does not require globally disabling pinch zoom.

Changed legacy pairing command codes from single-use to reusable for multiple devices until their existing 10-minute expiry; each paired device still receives its own independent 90-day signed owner token.
Stopped wrong-answer feedback from opening the owner/team Settings dialog on unpaired or expired devices; expired feedback authorization now asks the user to re-ask the question instead.
Changed Ask BallerWatch autocomplete back to a floating glass overlay under the input, with bounded scrolling, so suggestions no longer stretch or squeeze the Ask card.
Updated privacy documentation: anonymous Q&A is still not retained by default; the exact exchange is retained encrypted for up to 48 hours only if the visitor explicitly marks that answer wrong.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.6.0.

releases.title: iPhone-first BallerWatch dashboard refresh
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch 5.5 brings a new iPhone-first glass dashboard with a larger match spotlight, RSVP progress, brighter calendar selection, a polished Ask panel, and a floating notification inbox.
changes: Reworked the PWA visual system to match the approved iPhone-first demo direction while preserving the existing public/private behavior and interaction model.
Made the match spotlight date-first, added a dedicated pickup RSVP progress bar with spots-left status, strengthened weather presentation, and kept Directions/Share as large pill actions.
Restyled the 14-day calendar with brighter selected dates, clearer game indicators, and more compact glass tiles while preserving connected swipe navigation.
Refreshed Ask BallerWatch with a rounded search control, integrated answer surface, and stronger mobile hierarchy without changing Q&A routing or feedback behavior.
Changed the notification inbox into a floating frosted-glass popover while preserving unread tracking, push controls, full-screen reading, and swipe deletion.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.5.0 so existing Home Screen clients refresh to the new interface.

releases.title: Concise README highlights and live web demo
changes: Condensed the README release summary into five prominent grouped version highlights instead of listing every patch release.
Added a live BallerWatch web-app demo section with a direct launch link and a short guided flow for carousel, calendar, notifications, Q&A, and iPhone PWA behavior.
Aligned remaining README privacy wording with the current encrypted 48-hour original owner Q&A review design.
Kept runtime code, PWA assets, scheduling, notifications, and service-worker cache unchanged because this release is documentation-only.

releases.title: Current documentation alignment
changes: Updated README to describe the implemented double-tap/double-click wrong-answer feedback toggle instead of the retired long-press gesture.

Updated README to match the v5.4 encrypted review design: original owner question/answer text remains encrypted for at most 48 hours, while the readable review index contains only sanitized engineering signals.
Kept runtime code, PWA assets, notification behavior, and service-worker cache unchanged because this release corrects documentation only.

releases.title: Compact carousel, exact review source, and review-driven fixes
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now sizes match cards from the true tallest match, contains long opened notifications, retains exact encrypted review Q&A, and answers weekday time/location questions deterministically.
changes: Changed equal carousel sizing to measure only clean rendered match cards, excluding transient hint/error text that could make every card unnecessarily tall.
Kept every outgoing/incoming carousel card at the same width and true tallest-match height for the current viewport.
Contained the full-screen notification reader horizontally and made long URLs/unbroken notification text wrap inside the individual opened notification card.
Changed encrypted 48-hour owner chat history to retain the original question and original bot answer as the review source; Groq summaries/classifications remain separate metadata only.
Kept state/chat-review.json privacy-minimized and readable with only sanitized engineering signals, never raw question/answer text.
Expanded authenticated web feedback capture limits and preserved original whitespace/text before encrypted persistence.

Fixed the runtime-state negative-feedback issue where weekday time/location questions such as 'Thursday time' could fall through to a broad AI schedule answer; both legacy messaging/listener and Worker fast paths now route them deterministically to pickup details first.

Re-audited weather behavior: Open-Meteo uses America/Los_Angeles hourly data and only slots overlapping the actual match start/end window are summarized; existing regression tests reject whole-day/out-of-window rain spikes and cover overnight matches.
Rechecked runtime-state request indexes: there are no open explicit feature requests, and the single readable negative-feedback signal is addressed by this release.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.4.0.

releases.title: Historical notification-board deduplication
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now collapses older identical notification-board entries, keeping only the newest copy while preserving genuinely changed updates.
changes: Deduplicates notification-board results after newest-first sorting using channel, tag, title, body, and URL as the visible payload identity.
Keeps the newest copy of an identical historical notification and hides older duplicates already stored in runtime state.
Preserves entries whose visible content changed, even when they belong to the same pickup date/tag.
Complements 5.3.4, which already stopped new unchanged pickup reminders and duplicate Web Push creation.
Added regression coverage for historical board deduplication.

releases.title: Duplicate pickup notification suppression
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now suppresses unchanged pickup reminder notifications and prevents identical web-board entries from creating another push.
changes: Removed time-only hourly and 15-minute pickup reminders when the underlying match state has not changed.
Pickup notifications now require a meaningful change in RSVP/capacity, roster, location, primary match selection, or owner status.
Added a second dedupe guard in shared web notifications: identical tag/title/body/URL payloads reuse the existing board entry instead of creating a new entry or Web Push event.
Kept the two-minute pickup refresh cadence unchanged so monitoring remains fast without generating duplicate notifications.
Added regression coverage for unchanged pickup suppression and duplicate web-board/Web Push suppression.

releases.title: Equal carousel dimensions and weather-window verification
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch carousel cards now stay the same size across matches, with stronger verification that weather reflects each game's actual start/end window.
changes: Measures every available match card at the current viewport width and locks the carousel to the maximum required card height so all outgoing and incoming cards have identical dimensions.
Recomputes the shared card dimension after calendar refreshes and screen-size/orientation changes.
Removed pair-specific height changes during swipes so the carousel no longer grows or shrinks between neighboring games.
Verified that weather requests use America/Los_Angeles and that only hourly Open-Meteo slots overlapping the actual match start/end window are included.
Strengthened weather regression coverage so higher rain probabilities outside the match window are ignored.
Added overnight-match coverage to verify weather selection correctly crosses midnight.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.3.3.

releases.title: Connected-card match carousel
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch match swiping now behaves like connected cards on one track: the current and next/previous game cards move together smoothly as you swipe.
changes: Replaced the fixed-frame content swipe with a true two-card horizontal carousel.
Pre-renders the adjacent game as a separate full glass card beside the current card before it enters view.
Moves the outgoing and incoming cards together with a fixed gap so the gesture feels like connected train cars rather than a page shift or content swap.
Completes the same continuous motion after release, then synchronizes the selected calendar date and multi-match picker when the incoming card settles.
Keeps empty dates skipped, preserves vertical scrolling, ignores swipes that begin on Directions or Share, and eases back smoothly at the first or last game date.
Added regression coverage for paired card transforms, pre-rendered neighbor cards, carousel clipping, and synchronized calendar selection.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.3.2.

releases.title: Fixed-frame match swipe animation
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch swipe navigation now keeps the match card frame fixed while only the match content moves, eliminating the page-sliding feel on iPhone.
changes: Changed horizontal calendar swipe animation so the glass spotlight card itself never translates or fades.
Added an inner spotlight swipe surface so only match content follows the finger while the card border/background remains stationary.
Suppress horizontal page overscroll while a match swipe is actively recognized, while preserving normal vertical scrolling.
Kept Directions and Share controls excluded from swipe capture.
Added regression coverage that prevents transforms or opacity animation from being applied directly to the match card.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.3.1.

releases.title: Swipe navigation between calendar game dates
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch match cards can now be swiped left or right to move between game dates while the 14-day calendar highlight stays synchronized.
changes: Added horizontal swipe navigation to the main match spotlight on touch devices.
Swipe left selects the next date in the 14-day calendar that has a published game; swipe right selects the previous game date.
Empty dates are skipped so swipe navigation mirrors the existing clickable game-date behavior rather than showing blank match cards.
The selected calendar highlight and same-day multi-match picker stay synchronized with the swiped-to match.
Horizontal dragging follows the finger and transitions the newly selected match back into place; vertical scrolling remains available.
Swipes that start on interactive Directions or Share controls are ignored so normal button taps remain reliable.
Added regression coverage for swipe direction, game-date selection, calendar highlight synchronization, and touch behavior.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.3.0.

releases.title: Notification popup and sharing polish
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now uses generic Share, keeps the notification popup contained on iPhone, animates swipe-to-delete, and adds a subtle local Delete all action.
changes: Changed Send to Tesla back to a generic Share action so the iOS share sheet can expose whichever apps are actually available, including Tesla when present.
Restored full game details plus the map link in the native share payload and clipboard fallback.
Bound the notification dialog and made the history list independently scrollable so long notification history cannot overflow the popup controls.
Added interactive swipe-left motion that follows the finger, then slides and collapses the notification before local deletion.
Added a subtle Delete all action beside Send test that clears notification history only on the current device.
Added regression coverage for generic sharing, bounded notification layout, animated swipe deletion, and local Delete all.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.2.1.

releases.title: Notification inbox and Tesla destination sharing
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now has compact unread notifications with full-screen reading and swipe-to-delete, a smaller push toggle, Tesla destination sharing, and a legacy messaging footer shortcut.
changes: Changed the notification popup into a compact inbox with truncated previews and stable local per-device read/deleted state.
Opening a notification marks it read, opens a full-screen reader, and immediately decreases the bell badge because the badge now counts only unread non-deleted entries.
Added swipe-left deletion that hides a notification locally on the current device without mutating the shared public notification-board history.
Moved Web Push enable/disable into a smaller On/Off slider beside Refresh in the notification header while retaining the local notification test.
Changed the match Share action to Send to Tesla and optimized the iOS share payload for Tesla's supported Share-to-car flow; clipboard/Tesla-app fallback is used when native sharing is unavailable.
Added a legacy messaging footer shortcut beside GitHub and Wiki.
Added regression coverage for unread counts, full-screen notification reading, swipe deletion, compact push controls, Tesla sharing, and the legacy messaging shortcut.
Bumped the installed PWA shell and service-worker cache to 5.2.0.

releases.title: Reliable first launch after PWA releases
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch no longer gets stuck on loading placeholders on the first Home Screen launch after a release; live data now loads without the service-worker update race.
changes: Diagnosed the first-launch placeholder state as a startup race: service-worker registration/update could delay live data hydration, while controllerchange could reload the page before initialization finished.
Run service-worker registration and config, notification-board, and calendar hydration concurrently so slow iOS service-worker work cannot block visible match data.

If a new worker takes control during initial startup, defer the forced reload instead of interrupting hydration; the current screen finishes loading and the update is picked up on a later foreground or launch.
Preserve automatic reload behavior for service-worker updates discovered after initial startup.
Added regression coverage for the first-load update handoff and bumped the installed PWA shell.

releases.title: Autocomplete, feedback toggle, and schedule-aware weather
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch autocomplete no longer overlays nearby text, answer feedback toggles by double-click/tap, and weather refreshes immediately when a match date/time/location changes.
changes: Moved question autocomplete into normal document flow so suggestions expand the Ask section instead of drawing over the content below it.
Changed wrong-answer feedback from long-press to double-click/double-tap: the first gesture queues negative feedback and the next identical gesture cancels it.
Added a stable private feedback identifier so cancellation removes the matching encrypted review entry and its sanitized review signal rather than only changing local UI state.
Diagnosed missing Wed 10/7 weather: the pickup game changed after the previous six-hour weather snapshot, so live schedule data was newer than weather state.
Pickup date/time/field/address changes now trigger one notification-silent weather refresh immediately; RSVP counts and roster changes are deliberately excluded.
League schedule/calendar changes also refresh weather after the new schedule is persisted.
The six-hour maintenance weather refresh remains as the periodic fallback, keeping normal forecast request volume low.
Bumped the PWA shell so installed Home Screen clients receive the interaction fixes.

releases.title: Live match expiry and automatic refresh
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now removes completed matches from Next Game by their Pacific end time, pulses the Live indicator, and refreshes data/app updates automatically while open.
changes: Fixed Next Game eligibility to use the match end time in America/Los_Angeles instead of keeping every game dated today until midnight.
Pickup matches use their published end time, with a three-hour fallback only when no end time exists; league matches use their normalized two-hour window.
The 14-day web calendar also drops completed games so the default spotlight advances naturally after a match ends.
Added a continuously pulsing Live dot while the app is online, with a distinct non-animated offline state.
The open PWA refreshes calendar and notification-board data every 60 seconds and immediately when returning to the foreground or reconnecting.
The PWA checks its service worker for a new deployed release every five minutes and on foreground/reconnect; skipWaiting/controllerchange reloads the app automatically when a new shell is available.
Explicitly selected future calendar games are preserved across background data refreshes instead of being reset to the default next game.
Bumped the PWA shell and added regression tests around current-match expiry and automatic updates.

releases.title: League weather fallback and pickup capacity
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now falls back to Seattle-area match weather when a RATS venue cannot be geocoded, and pickup spotlight details show reserved/capacity.
changes: Diagnosed missing Tue 10/6 weather as a location-resolution gap: weather refresh completed successfully, but one league venue did not resolve to coordinates.
Added a Seattle-area weather fallback only for Seattle RATS league games when exact venue geocoding is unavailable; exact venue coordinates remain preferred.
Marks fallback weather as approximate in runtime/web data and labels it Seattle-area in the PWA.
Added public-safe per-game weather refresh diagnostics so future missing weather can be traced by date/kind without exposing private roster data.
Pickup spotlight and Share text now include reserved/capacity such as 12 / 16 reserved.
Bumped the PWA shell so installed clients refresh to the corrected behavior.

releases.title: Typography normalization
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now uses a consistent native system font and normalized type scale across the Liquid Glass interface.
changes: Removed the unloaded Inter-first font declaration and standardized the PWA on the native system UI font stack.
Normalized caption, small text, metadata, body, control, and section-heading sizes instead of many one-off font sizes.
Replaced synthetic 650/750 font weights with standard 600/700 weights for more consistent rendering across Safari and the installed iPhone PWA.
Kept question/settings inputs at 16px to prevent iOS focus zoom.
Aligned typography for spotlight metadata, calendar labels/weather, Q&A, notifications, settings, footer, and multi-game selectors.
Bumped the PWA shell so installed clients refresh to the corrected typography.

releases.title: Liquid Glass match spotlight
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now uses a Liquid Glass-style interface, and tapping a game day reuses the main match spotlight for the selected game.
changes: Reworked the PWA visual system with translucent glass surfaces, backdrop blur, specular highlights, softer depth, glass controls, and a non-blur fallback.
Calendar game-day taps now update the existing top match spotlight with the selected game, weather, field, Directions, and Share instead of rendering a second detail section.
Disabled interaction on empty calendar days so the main spotlight always represents a real published game.
Added a compact pill selector only when multiple games occur on the same date; selecting a pill updates the same spotlight.
Preserved the default next-game spotlight on initial load and visually distinguishes a calendar-selected match.
Bumped versioned PWA assets and service-worker cache so installed Home Screen clients refresh to the redesigned interface.

releases.title: Weather bootstrap and exact forecast window
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch weather now requests exactly the 14 days shown in the calendar and refreshes once automatically after weather-related releases.
changes: Reduced Open-Meteo forecast_days from 16 to exactly 14 so the weather request matches the UI horizon and avoids unnecessary forecast volume.
Added a notification-silent Refresh match weather workflow that runs once after weather/runtime-path releases and remains manually dispatchable.
Kept recurring weather refresh inside the six-hour maintenance workflow; the bootstrap workflow adds no new recurring schedule.

releases.title: Two-week match weather dashboard
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now has a redesigned dashboard with a 14-day game calendar and match-window rain/weather, while the scheduler uses fewer unnecessary recurring jobs.
changes: Redesigned the PWA into a match-day dashboard with a stronger next-game spotlight, compact app header, cleaner Q&A/search surface, and responsive two-week calendar.
Added a 14-day calendar covering published pickup games with locations and monitored RATS league matches, with per-day game details and Google Maps directions.
Added six-hour match weather using Open-Meteo hourly forecasts: condition, average match-window temperature, and maximum rain probability during the actual scheduled game window.

Added conservative cached venue geocoding through OpenStreetMap Nominatim: only uncached public venues are queried, requests are spaced over one second apart, and failed venue lookups wait seven days before retry.
Stored weather/geocode runtime data only in encrypted state/weather.json and exposed a public-safe /web/calendar projection without roster or owner-private data.
Reduced cron-job.org primary schedules to pickup every 2 minutes and league every 5 minutes. The old listener and external watchdog schedules are explicitly retired/disabled.
Moved system watchdog/maintenance to a native GitHub Actions schedule every six hours and combined that maintenance run with the weather refresh.
Added Open-Meteo/OpenStreetMap attribution, weather/scheduler regression tests, and a versioned v5 PWA shell.

releases.title: Owner pairing reliability fix
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch owner pairing now consumes codes through the listener workflow and returns readable errors instead of iPhone “Load failed” failures.
changes: Removed the direct runtime-state write from the successful Cloudflare owner-pairing path.
Pair-code consumption now dispatches the existing listener workflow, which owns durable encrypted listener-state writes.
Added CORS-safe 503/401 JSON responses so iPhone shows a useful pairing error instead of the generic Safari/PWA “Load failed” message.
Added regression coverage to prevent pairing from reintroducing direct Worker writes.

releases.title: Inline mobile header actions
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now keeps the Settings gear and notification bell aligned on one row in the installed mobile app.
changes: Removed the narrow-screen rule that stacked header actions vertically.
Kept Settings and notification bell on one row in the installed iPhone PWA and mobile browser layout.
Bumped versioned PWA assets/service-worker cache so existing Home Screen installs refresh to the corrected layout.
Added regression coverage for the mobile header action layout.

releases.title: Wrong-answer feedback and sentence autocomplete
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch web Q&A now supports full-sentence autocomplete and owner-paired press-and-hold feedback when an answer is wrong.
changes: Added owner-paired press-and-hold feedback on the web answer card; holding for about 0.7 seconds queues the current question/answer as negative_feedback for the next review.
Kept review feedback protected by the existing owner capability token so anonymous public visitors cannot inject engineering-review signals.
Expanded Q&A autocomplete into full-sentence predictions ranked from typed prefixes, including partial-word matching and weekday-specific soccer questions.
Added desktop acceptance shortcuts for the top completion with Tab or Right Arrow while preserving tap and arrow/Enter selection.
Autocomplete stays local/deterministic and does not call AI providers on each keystroke.
Clarified that cron-job.org schedules pickup, league, and watchdog only; the GitHub listener remains event-driven for private-bot and owner-paired web events.
Bumped the PWA shell so installed Home Screen apps refresh to the new behavior.

releases.title: Owner-paired web settings and shared review history
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch web settings can now be securely paired to an owner device, and paired web Q&A joins the same privacy-minimized 48-hour review loop.
changes: Added a top-right Settings gear with owner pairing, current pickup RSVP name, current monitored league teams, and encrypted settings updates.
Added a six-digit legacy pairing command owner code flow. Pair codes are hashed in encrypted listener settings, expire after 10 minutes, and are consumed after successful pairing.
Paired devices receive a signed 90-day owner capability token stored only in local browser storage; anonymous web access remains read-only and cannot retrieve private owner settings.

Paired web Q&A now uses the same privacy-minimized 48-hour encrypted review-history pipeline as private bot conversations, including bug_candidate and feature_candidate classification. Anonymous web Q&A is not retained.
Owner settings writes are narrowly scoped to pickup RSVP name and monitored league teams and are dispatched through the existing encrypted listener/runtime-state workflow.
Reduced the notification test UI to a subtle text action and shortened the local test-notification content.
Updated architecture, privacy, web-app, and onboarding documentation for the v4 owner-pairing boundary.

releases.title: Command suggestions and two-hour league windows
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch web Q&A now supports slash commands and autosuggestions, the app layout is cleaner, and league games without a published end time use a two-hour window.
changes: Removed the standalone main-page Push notifications card; enable/disable now lives only in the notification bell slider.
Moved Home Screen installation help to a compact footer section for browser visits while keeping it hidden in the installed Home Screen app.
Added a slash-command dropdown and natural-language autosuggestions to the one-question/one-answer box, with tap and keyboard selection.
Added read-only web shortcuts for /today, /next, /teams, /count [day], /field [day], /time [day], /version, and /help.
Removed legacy messaging references from app-facing HTML and manifest description.
Changed the RATS fallback duration from one hour to two hours when the source does not publish an end time, and updated Calendar explanatory text and tests.
Bumped the versioned PWA shell so installed devices refresh to the new interface.

releases.title: Next game card and closed-app notification test
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now shows the next upcoming game with Directions/Share and includes a safe notification test for the iPhone Home Screen app.
changes: Added a public-safe Next game card that selects the earliest upcoming pickup or RATS game using the same runtime data and ordering used by the existing fast path.
Added a Google Maps Directions button using the published field/address and a native device Share action with clipboard fallback.
Added a manual Test notification control in the bell panel that schedules a local service-worker notification after five seconds so the app can be closed before the alert appears.
Kept automated tests and smoke runs notification-silent: the manual notification test does not send Web Push signals or create notification-board entries.
Added a read-only /web/next-game endpoint, privacy regression coverage, UI tests, and a new versioned PWA shell so installed Home Screen apps receive the feature.

releases.title: Bell push notification switch
releases.webAnnouncement: The BallerWatch notification bell now includes a quick Push notifications switch that stays synchronized with the full Settings controls.
changes: Added a compact Push notifications on/off switch to the top-right notification bell panel.
The bell switch uses the same Web Push subscribe/unsubscribe path as Settings, so both surfaces stay synchronized with the device's real browser subscription.
Disabled the quick switch when Web Push is unsupported or notification permission is blocked, while preserving the existing Home Screen installation guidance on iPhone.
Bumped versioned PWA assets and the offline shell cache so installed Home Screen apps receive the new control without reinstalling.

releases.title: Reliable installed-app refresh
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch Home Screen installs now refresh new web-app releases more aggressively instead of staying on stale cached assets.
changes: Versioned the deployed CSS, JavaScript, and service-worker URLs so each PWA release has cache-distinct static assets.
Registered the service worker with updateViaCache disabled, explicitly checks for updates, and reloads once when a new worker takes control.
Changed same-origin service-worker network requests to bypass stale HTTP cache before updating the offline shell.
Added regression coverage for versioned assets, forced service-worker refresh, controller-change reload, and no-store fetch behavior.

releases.title: Installed app navigation
releases.webAnnouncement: The BallerWatch Home Screen app now hides installation help, opens recent updates from a top-right bell, and keeps push controls in Settings at the bottom.
changes: Hide and remove the Home Screen installation section whenever BallerWatch is already running as an installed standalone app, while retaining install help for normal browser visits.
Moved the recent notification board out of the main page into a top-right bell button that opens a dedicated notification dialog with refresh and close controls.
Moved Web Push enable/disable controls into a Settings section at the bottom of the app so the primary screen stays focused on Q&A.
Bumped the PWA shell cache generation so existing Home Screen installs refresh the redesigned HTML, JavaScript, and CSS instead of remaining on cached v3.0.x assets.
Added regression coverage for standalone install-card removal, bell navigation, Settings placement, and the new PWA cache generation.

releases.title: Least-privilege GitHub Pages activation
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch web app deployment now follows GitHub's standard Pages activation path without requiring an admin-level automation token.
changes: Removed the failed attempt to self-enable GitHub Pages with CRON_GITHUB_PAT; GitHub requires repository Administration-write in addition to Pages-write for that operation.

Changed the Pages workflow to detect whether the site is activated, report the exact one-time Settings step when it is not, and avoid turning that external setup requirement into a failed release workflow.
After one-time GitHub Pages activation, deployment uses the normal workflow-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN with pages: write and id-token: write rather than broadening the general automation PAT.
Added regression coverage and updated PWA/operations documentation for the least-privilege activation flow.

releases.title: Automatic Pages enablement and push-reset recovery
releases.webAnnouncement: The BallerWatch web app deployment now enables GitHub Pages automatically and Web Push recovers cleanly after a factory reset.
changes: Changed the GitHub Pages deployment to self-enable Pages using the existing CRON_GITHUB_PAT when no Pages site has been configured yet, avoiding a manual Settings step when the token has sufficient permission.
Added deployment verification for the live Cloudflare PWA API surface in addition to the existing legacy messaging webhook/health verification.
Changed PURGE to recreate a fresh empty encrypted VAPID identity immediately after clearing subscriptions and board state so the PWA can be re-enabled without another deployment.
Made the installed PWA detect a rotated VAPID application key, discard its stale browser subscription, and guide the user to enable push again.

releases.title: iPhone web app and Web Push fallback
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now has an installable iPhone web app with a notification board, read-only Q&A, and Web Push fallback when legacy messaging is unavailable.
changes: Added an installable GitHub Pages PWA at vudh1.github.io/ballerwatch with an iPhone Home Screen experience, offline app shell, dedicated touch icon, notification board, and one-question/one-answer read-only Q&A.

Added standards-based Web Push without a new database or notification provider: VAPID keys and browser subscriptions are generated/managed by GitHub Actions and stored AES-GCM encrypted on runtime-state.

Added Cloudflare Worker endpoints for public-safe web configuration, board reads, read-only Q&A, and encrypted subscribe/unsubscribe registration while keeping state-changing commands on legacy messaging.

Extended the existing pickup, real RATS schedule-change, and daily version notification allowlist to a legacy messaging-independent Web Push channel; legacy messaging delivery failure no longer prevents the public-safe fallback from being recorded and signaled.
Kept Workers KV absent, Cloudflare Cron Triggers disabled, cron-job.org as the 2/5/10-minute scheduler, and the single-parentless runtime-state snapshot model unchanged.
Added privacy regression coverage proving the public web path strips RSVP/waitlist names, owner settings, secrets, and private push material.

releases.title: Automatic GitHub Wiki synchronization
releases.webAnnouncement: The repository Wiki now stays synchronized automatically with the canonical docs/wiki documentation.
changes: Made docs/wiki the single source of truth for the GitHub Wiki and removed the separate WIKI_TOKEN dependency.
Changed the Publish wiki workflow to use the repository GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write and mirror docs/wiki on every relevant main update.
Updated current documentation so Wiki publishing behavior matches the automated workflow.

releases.title: Unified Node.js runtime
releases.webAnnouncement: BallerWatch now uses one Node.js runtime for league automation, Calendar reconciliation, tests, and notifications while preserving existing behavior.
changes: Migrated the six remaining league runtime Python modules and their tests to dependency-free Node.js ECMAScript modules.
Removed Python files, Python setup, compilation, unittest discovery, and Python invocations from GitHub Actions.
Preserved existing RATS tracking keys and Calendar fingerprints with Python-compatible canonical hashing plus Pacific DST behavior.
Added Node parity coverage for RATS normalization/retries, Calendar gate/pair/purge/sync, legacy messaging schedule notifications, and Apps Script in-place event updates.
Kept production architecture, runtime-state encryption, Calendar targeting, cron-job.org scheduling, and legacy messaging notification policy unchanged.

releases.title: RATS transient-source resilience
releases.webAnnouncement: RATS schedule refresh is now more resilient to temporary source outages while preserving verified Calendar state.
changes: Retry only transient RATS source failures with bounded exponential backoff, while permanent authentication/configuration errors fail immediately.
When a valid last-good league schedule already exists, retain it during transient RATS outages instead of failing the production watcher or applying unverified Calendar/legacy messaging changes.
Added a regression that executes the Apps Script update path and proves an existing tracked Calendar event is updated in place rather than duplicated.
Corrected current purge documentation to reflect that BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events are removed while unrelated Calendar events remain untouched.

releases.title: Index-independent Calendar pairing
releases.webAnnouncement: Calendar pairing no longer depends on Google Calendar search indexing, so a fresh target marker can be detected immediately.
changes: Changed Calendar target pairing to scan a bounded 21-day event window directly instead of relying on Google Calendar full-text search indexing.
Pairing checks the default Calendar first, then other visible calendars, while preserving the unique-marker proof and private Calendar ID storage.

releases.title: Pair Calendar bridge to intended target
releases.webAnnouncement: Calendar sync is now privately paired to the intended Google Calendar instead of relying on the Apps Script owner's default calendar.
changes: Added private Calendar pairing so the Apps Script bridge targets the intended Google Calendar rather than blindly using the deployment owner's default calendar.
Pairing discovers a temporary non-sensitive marker across calendars visible to the Apps Script account, stores only the matched calendar ID in Script Properties, and deletes the marker after pairing.
Before switching targets, the bridge cleans BallerWatch-managed events and stale mappings from the previous target/default calendar to avoid orphaned wrong-calendar events.
Normal Calendar sync now fails closed until a target Calendar has been paired, and no Calendar ID or email is committed or logged.
Moved all unit and smoke test-only code into a dedicated tests/ tree that mirrors source areas, leaving production folders runtime-only.
Condensed README release notes to a short recent-changes section while keeping complete release history in features/versions.json.

releases.title: Stale Calendar mapping cleanup
releases.webAnnouncement: Calendar purge now treats mappings to already-deleted events as harmless stale state instead of failing the full reset.
changes: Changed Calendar PURGE so Script Property mappings to events that no longer exist or were already deleted are cleared as stale state rather than treated as fatal errors.
Kept all other Calendar deletion, permission, API, and marker-scan errors fail-closed.
Added stale-mapping counts to purge logs and regression coverage for the reporting path.

releases.title: Calendar purge reliability fix
releases.webAnnouncement: Calendar reset is now more resilient and verifies the deployed bridge version before deleting BallerWatch-managed match events.
changes: Hardened Calendar purge so one stale or inaccessible event cannot abort deletion of all other BallerWatch-managed events.
Changed the legacy marker safety scan to bounded yearly Calendar queries and added safe bridge error reporting for operational debugging.
Required the live Apps Script Calendar bridge to report version 3 or newer before a full reset can run.
Added regression coverage for surfaced Calendar purge errors.

releases.title: Full reset and workflow cleanup
releases.webAnnouncement: Full reset now clears BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events as well as runtime state, and obsolete maintenance workflows were removed.
changes: Expanded PURGE so it deletes only BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events through the authenticated Apps Script bridge before clearing runtime-state.
Added a safe Calendar purge action that removes tracked event IDs and marker-tagged legacy BallerWatch events without touching unrelated Calendar events.
Removed the obsolete Configure repository and Seed failover cache workflows; production watchers already maintain failover caches and repository configuration is no longer a recurring operation.
Added Calendar bridge syntax validation and Calendar purge client tests.
Added a one-time release reset hook so this release can deploy the new Calendar bridge, purge Calendar/runtime state, and let the normal 2/5/10-minute production watchers rebuild from scratch.

releases.title: Quiet legacy messaging notification policy
releases.webAnnouncement: legacy messaging is now quiet by default: only RSVP watcher alerts, direct answers, one combined daily version update, and real league schedule changes are sent.
changes: Restricted proactive legacy messaging output to RSVP watcher notifications, real league schedule changes, and a single combined version announcement per Pacific day; direct replies to user questions remain unchanged.
Made watchdog failures, watchdog recovery, CI/testing/build activity, unsolicited setup reminders, invalid-setting reminders, and score-only changes silent on legacy messaging.
Combined every not-yet-announced release into one daily version message using user-facing release summaries instead of commit, pull-request, or other engineering details.
Changed league Calendar fingerprints so score-only changes do not trigger schedule reconciliation or legacy messaging schedule-update messages.
Removed the standalone legacy messaging score notifier.

releases.title: Self-healing pickup endpoint
changes: Added a privacy-safe recovery path that rediscovers the current public RSVP Apps Script endpoint when the configured endpoint is missing or retired with HTTP 404/410.
Kept encrypted endpoint overrides and the UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT secret as the primary configuration; discovered endpoint values are never committed, logged, or persisted to runtime state.
Added endpoint extraction/recovery regression tests and verified the live notification-silent pickup smoke succeeds with the stale configured secret.
Extended stale-branch cleanup to remove inactive fix/* branches as well as release/* branches.

releases.title: Runtime-only snapshot tree
changes: Restricted runtime-state root snapshots to the canonical generated runtime paths instead of carrying the repository source tree into the snapshot branch.
Kept the one-parentless-commit retention model and optimistic concurrent-writer protection introduced in 2.5.4.
Expanded runtime-state regression coverage so PURGE produces an empty root tree and a rebuilt snapshot contains only the expected runtime file.

releases.title: Single-snapshot runtime-state retention
changes: Changed runtime-state persistence so each successful write replaces branch history with one parentless snapshot commit containing only the current encrypted runtime files.
Made PURGE compact runtime-state to the same one-commit form while preserving optimistic concurrency with the existing retry behavior.
Added regression coverage proving both a purge and a subsequent state rebuild leave runtime-state with exactly one root commit.
Added automatic cleanup of stale release branches that no longer have an open pull request.

releases.title: Chat-review-driven schedule question fixes
changes: Used privacy-minimized 48-hour chat-review signals to identify recurring failures for today's schedule, specific-date schedules, pickup details, and next/recommended-game wording.
Added deterministic routing and date-aware schedule lookup across both pickup and RATS league data so common read-only questions are answered from existing runtime state before AI.
Expanded bounded Gemini/Groq fallback context with upcoming league matches while keeping private participant data out of prompts.
Added regression tests for the reviewed natural-language phrasings and date-specific fast-path schedule replies.

releases.title: Webhook-only legacy messaging listener hardening
changes: Removed the GitHub listener's legacy legacy messaging getUpdates fallback so empty workflow dispatches no-op instead of conflicting with the active Cloudflare webhook.
Processed Cloudflare fast-path history-only dispatches directly before legacy messaging update handling, fixing failed history persistence runs after the runtime purge.
Made primary cron-job.org scheduler synchronization explicitly disable any legacy legacy messaging listener polling schedule whenever the management API is available.

releases.title: Optional cron-job.org management API during quota exhaustion
changes: Made the post-merge cron-job.org setup workflow tolerate only temporary management API failures such as HTTP 429/502/503/504 or network timeouts, while authentication errors remain blocking.

Made legacy messaging Worker deployment independent of temporary cron-job.org management API availability after the Worker, secrets, webhook, health check, and zero-Cloudflare-Cron verification have succeeded.
Kept scheduler correctness fail-closed whenever cron-job.org responds: missing, disabled, duplicated, mistargeted, or wrong-cadence jobs still fail verification.

releases.title: Gemini Flash-first answers and safer runtime recovery
changes: Added Gemini Flash as the preferred bounded natural-language answer provider, with Groq fallback and deterministic/non-AI handling when AI is unavailable or unsuitable.

Preserved the KV-free 2.4 architecture: Cloudflare remains webhook plus read-only fast path, cron-job.org remains the 2/5/10-minute scheduler, and encrypted durable runtime state remains on the runtime-state branch.
Hardened PURGE and clean bootstrap behavior so an available runtime-state branch is authoritative and deleted files cannot be resurrected from legacy Cloudflare or stale Actions-cache backups.
Reduced recurring cron-job.org management API verification to four reads per day while keeping the watchdog itself at 10-minute cadence.

Made temporary cron-job.org management API unavailability such as HTTP 429 non-blocking for release smoke, while authenticated scheduler misconfiguration, missing jobs, disabled jobs, or wrong cadences still fail verification.

Made notification-silent release smoke tolerate only transient RATS source outages when a valid last-good schedule is already present; schema, auth, configuration, and invalid-state failures still block the release.

releases.title: Explicit Cloudflare Cron Trigger removal
changes: Fixed the 2.4.0 cutover so Wrangler explicitly publishes triggers.crons=[]; omitting the property leaves previously deployed Cloudflare Cron Triggers in place.
Added a deployment verification step that reads the Cloudflare Worker schedules API and fails unless the ballerwatch-legacy messaging Worker has zero Cron Triggers after deployment.

releases.title: KV-free runtime and 48-hour chat review
changes: Removed Workers KV and Cloudflare Cron Triggers from the production runtime to eliminate the daily KV request-limit risk; Cloudflare now hosts only the legacy messaging webhook and read-only fast path with short-lived Cache API use.

Made cron-job.org the primary 2/5/10-minute scheduler and moved durable generated state to a dedicated runtime-state Git branch, with private runtime payloads remaining AES-GCM encrypted and main staying release-oriented.
Added one-time migration from the existing Cloudflare KV runtime into the runtime-state branch before the KV binding is removed, while retaining encrypted GitHub Actions cache as a recovery source.

Replaced automatic feature-request creation for unanswered questions and thumbs-down feedback with a 48-hour Groq-condensed encrypted legacy messaging history and privacy-minimized bug/feature/negative-feedback review signals.
Kept the legacy messaging fast path lightweight by persisting condensed history asynchronously to the runtime-state branch after the reply, using the GitHub listener only as a persistence fallback.

releases.title: Cloudflare empty-KV self-bootstrap
changes: Made Cloudflare league refresh recover from empty or freshly purged KV by bootstrapping the built-in monitored-team defaults and rediscovering the current RATS season.
Centralized non-secret default league-team configuration so GitHub and Cloudflare use the same bootstrap values.
Changed GitHub Wiki publishing to wait gracefully for an optional write-capable WIKI_TOKEN instead of failing main when GitHub's normal Actions token cannot initialize the separate wiki repository.

releases.title: Resilient failover and onboarding foundation
changes: Standardized repository code style and module-level documentation, added a dependency-free style checker, expanded CI coverage, and added long-form onboarding/operations documentation under docs/wiki.

Kept all three cron-job.org failover jobs enabled at their 2/5/10-minute cadences while adding a Cloudflare heartbeat gate so pickup and league fallback runs skip duplicate source work when the edge is healthy.
Added encrypted GitHub Actions cache backups of last-known pickup, league, and watchdog runtime state so GitHub fallback can continue when the Worker runtime-state API is unavailable.
Changed PURGE into a full Cloudflare KV runtime factory reset, including custom league-team state; built-in default teams bootstrap again on the next league run.
Added a deterministic intent/tag index before Groq to reduce AI calls and edge latency for common natural-language questions.
Centralized runtime path definitions and persisted the fresh Cloudflare RATS change signal so full league reconciliation can skip a duplicate aggregate API request after edge-triggered changes.
Added a GitHub Wiki publishing workflow and documented architecture, failover, development, operations, release process, and data/privacy boundaries.

releases.title: Release-oriented repo and faster league reconciliation
changes: Cleaned obsolete runtime and scheduler files after the Cloudflare KV migration, including the legacy league status artifact and superseded cron management helpers.

Reduced RATS reconciliation latency by trying the last known valid season first, fetching independent team schedule exports concurrently, and removing unnecessary Node/Python setup steps from the production league workflow.

Added cron-job.org fallback verification: pickup, league and watchdog fallback jobs must exist with their expected 2/5/10-minute cadences, correct workflow targets, and remain disabled while Cloudflare is healthy.
Unified cron-job.org fallback creation, verification, enable and disable behavior in one tested module.
Adopted release branches with notification-silent PR smoke tests and squash-only merges so future main history is one commit per released version.
Serialized release-PR live smoke tests to avoid duplicate upstream traffic and added league watcher timing output for performance regression tracking.

releases.title: KV-only runtime state
changes: Migrated all remaining listener, pickup, league, Calendar, watchdog and feature-request runtime state from tracked repository files into the private Cloudflare KV namespace.
Removed all 12 runtime-state files from GitHub and changed the privacy audit to fail if those runtime paths are ever tracked again.
Updated listener, pickup, league and watchdog workflows to pull state from KV at startup, push updated state back to KV, clean the local runner copy, and never commit runtime data.
Moved manual data purge to Cloudflare KV and updated the notification-silent smoke test to use KV runtime fixtures.
Added protected Worker runtime-state APIs, a public privacy-safe feature-summary endpoint, fast-reply state synchronization, and deployment round-trip verification for all runtime scopes.
Removed the production fallback that read runtime soccer state from GitHub; Cloudflare KV is now the sole runtime-state authority.

releases.title: Cloudflare-first runtime
changes: Cut over recurring pickup, RATS and health checks from cron-job.org/GitHub Actions polling to Cloudflare Cron Triggers with private KV hot state.
Common legacy messaging read-only questions now stay on the Cloudflare fast path with structured deterministic intent handling, bounded Groq intent classification and short conversation context.

Cloudflare performs lightweight source change detection and dispatches GitHub pickup/league reconciliation only when data changes; GitHub remains responsible for CI, deployment, durable encrypted repository state, Calendar reconciliation and state-changing fallback commands.

Added notification-silent live source verification and KV priming before edge activation, stable webhook authentication, serialized Worker deployments and automatic cron-job.org fallback restoration if an edge deployment fails.
Moved watchdog health semantics from GitHub workflow freshness to Cloudflare KV/source heartbeats and hardened source fingerprints so failed reconciliation dispatches are retried.

releases.title: Cloudflare primary-runtime preview
changes: Added a Cloudflare scheduled edge runtime for 2-minute pickup checks, 5-minute RATS checks, and 10-minute health/deep-watchdog coordination.
Added private Cloudflare KV hot-state support for current soccer snapshots, conversation context, AI budget, fingerprints and scheduler health.
Edge polling dispatches the existing GitHub pickup/league workflows only when source data changes, moving routine GitHub Actions out of the normal polling hot path after cutover.
Added notification-silent shadow refresh verification before legacy cron-job.org schedules are disabled.
Added dynamic KV provisioning with a manual CLOUDFLARE_KV_NAMESPACE_ID fallback, plus Worker bundle and edge-runtime regression tests.
Activation remains gated until Cloudflare KV access is available; failed cutover verification leaves the existing cron-job.org production schedules active.

releases.title: Cloudflare fast path and AI intent routing
changes: Added a Cloudflare read-only fast path that answers common legacy messaging questions directly from encrypted GitHub state without starting a GitHub Actions runner.
Added short-lived conversation context so follow-up questions such as 'what field?', 'what time?' and 'how many?' can refer to the previously discussed pickup date.
Added Groq intent classification at the edge for natural-language read-only questions while keeping facts and actions deterministic.
Split the free AI budget into 25 edge classifications and 25 GitHub fallback calls per UTC day.
Stored private AI feature-request classification metadata for later improvement without publishing request text.

releases.title: Private feature requests
changes: Replaced public request text, IDs and timestamps with an allowlisted category/count summary; original requests remain encrypted.
Added request privacy regression tests, strict public-summary schema validation and a listener audit before state commits.
Preserved encrypted request archives on decryption failure and documented dedicated-key migration requirements.

releases.title: Direct-main maintenance and silent testing
changes: Allowed validated repository maintenance changes to commit directly to main again and removed the PR-only governance requirement.
Made the manual smoke test notification-silent: it verifies refreshed pickup and league data without sending legacy messaging messages or changing Google Calendar.
Removed default monitored team names from README while keeping the configured defaults in code.
Updated scheduled ChatGPT maintenance guidance to sync current repository instructions before changes and avoid legacy messaging notifications during testing.

releases.title: Manual data purge and protected main
changes: Added a manual Purge current data GitHub Action that clears generated pickup, league, Calendar-reconciliation, watchdog, and feature-request data while preserving configuration and secrets.
Added repository governance setup for a concise GitHub description and PR-only normal changes to main, with a narrow GitHub Actions bypass for encrypted runtime-state persistence.
Simplified README and agent guidance and required scheduled ChatGPT maintenance to sync from current main and use branch + pull request changes.

releases.title: Deleted Calendar event recovery
changes: Versioned league Calendar tracking keys so stale Apps Script event-ID mappings from manually deleted Calendar events are invalidated.
The Calendar bridge now falls back to matching an active event or creating a fresh event instead of reusing the previous tracking property.
Added regression coverage for the versioned Calendar tracking key.

releases.title: Concurrent state replay hardening
changes: Reworked workflow state persistence to replay generated encrypted state onto the latest main branch before each push attempt.
Prevents rebase conflicts from losing Calendar-applied league snapshots when listener, pickup, league, or watchdog workflows commit concurrently.

releases.title: Default league team bootstrap
changes: Added Third Touch FC and PhoSaiGon as built-in league defaults in that priority order for clean/fresh state.
Encrypted legacy messaging-managed league team state remains authoritative after bootstrap, so teams can still be added, removed, or renamed.
Purged previously retrieved pickup and league match snapshots before clean-bootstrap end-to-end testing.

releases.title: Calendar bridge deployment compatibility
changes: Updated the Apps Script deployment workflow to replace the Code.js filename produced by clasp pull, avoiding duplicate Code.js/Code.gs conflicts.
Verified the full Calendar bridge CI path: project pull, code push, existing deployment update, live webhook health check, and OAuth cleanup.

releases.title: One-time release announcements
changes: Replaced the single last-announcement marker with persisted announcement-ID history so each enabled release/feature announcement is delivered only once per stored bot state.
Historical announcements are marked seen during migration so older releases cannot rotate back into legacy messaging.
Cleared all currently stored public/redacted and encrypted/private feature suggestions.

releases.title: Concurrent state persistence hardening
changes: Added bounded pull/rebase/push retries to listener, pickup, league, and watchdog state persistence.
Prevents transient Git ref races between independently scheduled workflows from dropping otherwise successful runs.

releases.title: League team migration reliability
changes: Fixed legacy league-team migration so a valid legacy configuration replaces an existing empty encrypted placeholder.
Preserved the rule that only encrypted league-team state is persisted in BallerWatch.

releases.title: Operational setup runbooks
changes: Added an agent skill for safely discovering and verifying the pickup UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT without committing its live value.
Added repository agent guidance so future maintenance uses the endpoint-discovery procedure and preserves privacy.
Clarified that TRACKER_STATE_KEY is optional when the existing deployment uses the retired adapter token encryption fallback.
Expanded the validation workflow triggers so version history and operational guidance changes are validated automatically.

releases.title: Versioned release history
changes: Added a SemVer release ledger with current version and chronological change history.
legacy messaging feature announcements now include the release version.
Added /version and version commands to report the current release and latest changes.
Scheduled ChatGPT maintenance tasks must record a release entry whenever they change the product.

releases.title: Automated infrastructure provisioning
changes: Added idempotent cron-job.org API provisioning for listener, pickup, league, and watchdog workflows.
Added automated Google Apps Script Calendar bridge deployment using the existing deployment ID.
Hardened privacy checks against committing Apps Script OAuth/config credentials.

releases.title: BallerWatch consolidated baseline
changes: Consolidated pickup, league, legacy messaging, Calendar, watchdog, privacy, and feature-builder automation into BallerWatch.
Kept live soccer data and user configuration encrypted at rest.
Added watchdog recovery, manual smoke testing, and privacy-redacted feature requests.
